We have this impression from popular media of people getting shot and being knocked around by the impact, but the way physics works, when a bullet is fired, it doesn't generate any more forward momentum than it does backward momentum (recoil). A gun capable of knocking a person over would also knock over the person firing it - which is why big artillery is fired from mounts. You target shoot, so you know what recoil feels like - with a small handgun, just the strength of your wrist and hand is enough to contain the whole force of the recoil with basically just a twitch, and the impact of the bullet isn't significantly more forceful than that.

That second part has gotten away from us, however we can't apply justice solely at the whims of victims. We can't allow victims to apply their own justice.
